text: For torque-free rotation of a rigid body with distinct principal moments I₁ < I₂ < I₃, the tennis-racket (intermediate-axis) theorem states that steady rotation is:
choices: stable about all three principal axes
unstable about all three principal axes
stable about the smallest- and largest-moment axes, but unstable about the intermediate axis
stable only about the intermediate-moment axis
explanation: The book's tennis-racket theorem says torque-free rotation about the smallest (I₁) and largest (I₃) principal axes is stable, whereas rotation about the intermediate axis (I₂) is unstable and makes the body tumble. Rotation is therefore neither uniformly stable nor uniformly unstable, and the intermediate axis is precisely the unstable one — the opposite of the last option.
